label: History
value: Billina is a yellow hen
unit: Billina, a yellow hen who was raised on a farm in the United States, was named Bill as a chick by a young boy who mistook her gender. She first met Dorothy while floating in an ocean-bound hen-coop, after which the two drifted ashore, faced the hostile Wheelers, and discovered the mechanical man Tiktok. After traveling to the Land of Ev, Billina was briefly imprisoned in a chicken-house before being rescued by Dorothy and joining Princess Ozma's quest to free Ev's royal family from the Nome King. During the expedition, Billina secretly hid beneath the Nome King's throne, overheard how the captives were enchanted, and used her secret knowledge alongside the king's terror of eggs to break the enchantments on the prisoners. After helping the party defeat the Nome King and escape, she identified a tin pig whistle as the transformed Tin Woodman and restored him. Preferring Oz to Kansas, Billina chose to remain in the fairy kingdom when Dorothy went to Australia, eventually hatching ten chicks. She later re-encountered Dorothy, Tiktok, and other companions, traveling to the Emerald City to attend Princess Ozma's grand birthday banquet and festival.

label: Appearance
value: Bright is a small boy.
unit: Bright is a small, beautiful boy with a chubby round face, pretty curls all over his head, and big, blue, earnest eyes. At one point, he is transformed to have a hairy fox's head on his skinny shoulders, complete with a sharp nose, pointed ears, and keen little eyes, which he covers with a sailor hat with a gilt anchor on the band. He is dressed in sailor clothes consisting of wide trousers and a blouse with gold anchors on the broad collar, though he is also dressed in a blue-and-gold satin suit that makes him look as sweet as a cherub. His original round face, blue eyes, and curly head are later restored to his shoulders, replacing the fox head.

label: History
value: Button-Bright is a young boy.
unit: Button-Bright is a young, lost boy who is discovered digging a hole under a chestnut tree by Dorothy, Toto, and the Shaggy Man. Unsure of his background or home, he joins the travelers on their journey. Upon reaching Foxville, King Dox considers Button-Bright clever and transforms his head into that of a fox. Continuing down the road with his new fox head, he scares a group of donkeys at the gates of Dunkiton, though he and his friends are eventually allowed entry. After surviving an attack by head-hurling Scoodlers and crossing the Deadly Desert in a sand-boat, the group arrives in the Land of Oz. While exploring the Winkie Country, Button-Bright accidentally falls into the Truth Pond, which restores his head to its normal human form. He travels on to the Emerald City, where he winds up the mechanical man Tik-tok, meets Jack Pumpkinhead, and is dressed by Dorothy to meet Princess Ozma. Button-Bright attends Ozma's grand birthday festivities and banquet alongside human dignitaries, magical creatures, and animals before the celebration concludes.

label: Personality
value: The Woggle-Bug frequently makes puns.
unit: A pompous and learned figure, the Woggle-Bug frequently makes puns, finding the urge to express them nearly irresistible. Pacing in an absurd attempt to maintain a dignified demeanor, he serves as a Public Accuser whose vast knowledge prevents others from deceiving him. Driven by strategic ambition, he has advocated for laying siege to the city to starve it into submission.

label: History
value: Bug was originally an ordinary woggle-bug.
unit: Originally an ordinary woggle-bug, Bug gained education by listening to a schoolmaster from a secluded school-house hearth and became magnified after being displayed on a magnifying screen. After escaping to a grove of trees and saving a tailor's ninth life, he introduced himself as the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug to Tip and his companions, joining their trek to the Emerald City and suggesting how to repair the Saw-Horse. Along the journey, his puns annoyed the group, but he helped navigate magical obstacles, survive an attack by Jackdaws, and fix their flying Gump machine using a wishing pill. Bug accompanied the party to Glinda the Good's realm and witnessed Mombi break her enchantment to transform Tip back into Princess Ozma. He eventually took up residence in the Emerald City, later acting as the prosecutor during Eureka's trial after one of the Wizard's piglets went missing. He went on to compose an ode for Ozma's birthday as well as a waltz for the Tin Woodman, ultimately attending Princess Ozma's grand birthday banquet and festival alongside the royal court and distinguished guests.

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "I have never ceased to congratulate myself for escaping while I was Highly Magnified; for even my excessive knowledge would have proved of little use to me had I remained a tiny, insignificant insect."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: "If the Pumpkinhead is to ride, why not use one of his legs to make a leg for the horse that carries him? I judge that both are made of wood."

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “But you were the King until she came,” said the Woggle-Bug, strutting up and down with his hands in his pockets; “so it appears to me that she is the interloper instead of you.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “As for me,” said the Woggle-Bug, “I think that I could live for some time on Jack Pumpkinhead. Not that I prefer pumpkins for food; but I believe they are somewhat nutritious, and Jack’s head is large and plump.”

label: Quote
value: Bug said: “You have; and I’ve restrained a good many of them,” replied the insect. “But there are opportunities for so many excellent puns in our language that, to an educated person like myself, the temptation to express them is almost irresistible.”

label: Personality
value: Cowardly Lion is a self-described wild beast
unit: This character is a self-described wild beast who, despite being called a coward and feeling afraid of everything, considers himself as brave as any beast that ever lived. His primary motivation is to ask and receive courage from the Great Oz, desiring a specific kind of courage that allows him to forget his fear so he may truly become the King of Beasts. Known for his loyalty, kindness, and intelligence, his gentle nature helps reassure others upon meeting them. Nevertheless, he openly experiences fear when facing danger, falling, or encountering creatures like the Kalidahs. Ultimately, his unbearable struggle with fear drives his persistent quest to gain the courage he seeks.

label: History
value: The Lion believed he was born a coward.
unit: Believing he was born a coward, the Lion spent his early life roaring loudly at other creatures and men to scare them away, eventually coming to rule the great forest as the King of Beasts. While traveling, he attacked Dorothy and her companions; after Dorothy slapped his nose and called him a coward, he admitted his secret lack of courage and joined her journey to request courage from the Great Oz. Along the yellow brick road, he proved his loyalty by carrying his companions over a deep ditch and swimming their raft ashore, though he later fell victim to the sleep-inducing scarlet poppies until rescued by thousands of field mice. When the group reached the Emerald City, Oz appeared to the Lion as a terrifying Ball of Fire and demanded the destruction of the Wicked Witch of the West. During their quest, the Winged Monkeys captured the Lion, and the Witch imprisoned him and attempted to starve him until Dorothy secretly fed him and eventually destroyed the Witch. Upon returning to the Emerald City, the Lion received a liquid potion for courage from the humbug Wizard and later joined the expedition south to Glinda the Good Witch, decapitating a giant spider-like monster along the way to be crowned King of the Forest by its grateful animal inhabitants. Later, he joined Princess Ozma on an expedition to the Nome King's realm to rescue the royal family of Ev, actively defending Dorothy when the enraged King attempted to capture her. The Cowardly Lion eventually returned to the Emerald City, retaining part of the courage given to him by the Wizard, and served by pulling Ozma's royal chariot alongside the Hungry Tiger to transport Dorothy and her guests to the palace for Ozma's grand birthday celebration.

label: History
value: Dorothy is an orphan from a farm in Kansas.
unit: Dorothy is an orphan from a farm in Kansas who was carried to the Land of Oz by a severe cyclone, inadvertently crushing the Wicked Witch of the East upon landing. Given the Witch's silver shoes, she set out along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City to ask the Great Wizard Oz to send her home, befriending the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. After surviving a field of dangerous poppy flowers and reaching the Emerald City, Dorothy and her companions were commanded by the Wizard to slay the Wicked Witch of the West before he would grant their wishes. Dorothy was subsequently captured by the Witch's Winged Monkeys and forced into servitude, but she killed the Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. After returning to the Emerald City and discovering the Wizard was merely a human ventriloquist, Dorothy sought out Glinda the Good Witch, who revealed that the silver shoes possessed the power to take her back to Kansas. Years later, Dorothy was swept overboard during a storm at sea while traveling to Australia and washed ashore in Ev, where she met the mechanical man Tiktok and was briefly imprisoned by Princess Langwidere before being rescued by Princess Ozma. Joining Ozma's quest to free Ev's royal family from the Nome King, Dorothy stole the King's magic belt, which allowed her party to escape and return home safely. During a subsequent earthquake in California, Dorothy fell into an underground world with her kitten Eureka and a farm boy named Zeb, traveling through sub-terrestrial realms alongside the Wizard of Oz until Ozma used her magic belt to bring them to safety in the Emerald City. Made a Princess of Oz by Ozma, Dorothy returned home to Kansas once more, only to get lost on a later journey down a mysterious seventh road; accompanied by the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome, she navigated strange lands, crossed the Deadly Desert, and finally returned to the Emerald City to attend Ozma's grand birthday celebration before being transported home again.

After surviving a field of dangerous poppy flowers and reaching the Emerald City, Dorothy and her companions were commanded by the Wizard to slay the Wicked Witch of the West before he would grant their wishes. Dorothy was subsequently captured by the Witch's Winged Monkeys and forced into servitude, but she killed the Witch by throwing a bucket of water on her, causing her to melt. After returning to the Emerald City and discovering the Wizard was merely a human ventriloquist, Dorothy sought out Glinda the Good Witch, who revealed that the silver shoes possessed the power to take her back to Kansas. Years later, Dorothy was swept overboard during a storm at sea while traveling to Australia and washed ashore in Ev, where she met the mechanical man Tiktok and was briefly imprisoned by Princess Langwidere before being rescued by Princess Ozma. Joining Ozma's quest to free Ev's royal family from the Nome King, Dorothy stole the King's magic belt, which allowed her party to escape and return home safely. During a subsequent earthquake in California, Dorothy fell into an underground world with her kitten Eureka and a farm boy named Zeb, traveling through sub-terrestrial realms alongside the Wizard of Oz until Ozma used her magic belt to bring them to safety in the Emerald City. Made a Princess of Oz by Ozma, Dorothy returned home to Kansas once more, only to get lost on a later journey down a mysterious seventh road; accompanied by the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome, she navigated strange lands, crossed the Deadly Desert, and finally returned to the Emerald City to attend Ozma's grand birthday celebration before being transported home again.

label: History
value: King Dox rules Foxville
unit: King Dox rules Foxville and had longed all his life to visit the land of Oz. When Dorothy and her companions were brought before him, he welcomed them warmly and transformed Button-Bright's head into a fox's head as a reward, claiming he lacked the power to turn him back when asked. King Dox later traveled to the Emerald City as a royal guest to attend Princess Ozma's grand birthday banquet and festival before the foreign visitors departed.

label: Quote
value: Dox said: "Yes; it is to be the most brilliant royal ceremony ever held in any city in Fairyland, and I hope you will try to get me an invitation."

label: Quote
value: Dox said: "Be contented with your lot, whatever it happens to be, if you are wise. Which reminds me that you have a new companion on this adventure—he looks very clever and bright."

label: Quote
value: Dox said: "How should you? Well, I'll tell you. My private name is Dox, but a King can't be called by his private name; he has to take one that is official. Therefore my official name is King Renard the Fourth. Ren-ard with the accent on the 'Ren'."

label: Quote
value: Dox said: "I can't do that," he said; "I haven't the power, even if I wanted to. No, Button-Bright must wear his fox head, and he'll be sure to love it dearly as soon as he gets used to it."

label: Quote
value: Dox said: "Don't leave us yet, I beg of you," pleaded King Renard. "I intend to have several days of feasting and merry-making in honor of your visit."

label: History
value: Eureka is a kitten
unit: Eureka, a kitten found and named by Dorothy Gale, plummeted into a deep subterranean abyss alongside Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the cab-horse during a sudden earthquake. Landing in a underground glass city, Eureka gained the ability to speak and accompanied the group as they encountered the vegetable-like Mangaboo people. When the hostiles attempted to condemn the group's animals to the Black Pit, Eureka helped put up a fierce fight before eventually escaping a dark cave to fetch Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard of Oz to rescue her companions. She then traveled with the party across the water in the Valley of Voe, up Pyramid Mountain into the Country of the Gargoyles, and past a cavern of dragonettes. Trapped in a dead-end cave, Eureka was magically transported to the Emerald City alongside Dorothy when Princess Ozma used the Magic Belt. In Oz, Eureka was put on trial for murder when one of the Wizard's piglets went missing, acting defiant until she eventually revealed the missing piglet was alive and trapped inside a narrow vase in Ozma's room. Following her acquittal, Eureka returned home to Kansas with Dorothy via the Magic Belt.

label: History
value: General Jinjur spent her early life at home.
unit: Before rising to power, General Jinjur spent her early life at home making beds and washing dishes for her mother. Seeking a grander life, she organized an Army of Revolt made up entirely of young women and successfully captured the Emerald City. Her forces disarmed the guards, conquered the city without bloodshed, and drove the Scarecrow from the throne, after which Jinjur declared herself Queen and enlisted the witch Mombi to help defend her realm. After briefly losing control of the palace when the Scarecrow frightened her army with mice, Jinjur regained her footing until Glinda the Sorceress and Princess Ozma besieged the city. Jinjur fought a battle against Glinda's forces and steadfastly refused to step down, but she was ultimately captured during an aerial assault, conquered by Ozma, and removed from power. She later crossed paths again with Ozma's companions, meeting Dorothy Gale as the girl traveled across the desert on a magic carpet.

label: History
value: Glinda the Good granted an audience to Dorothy Gale and her companions at her palace.
unit: Glinda the Good, the beautiful Sorceress of the South who conquered the evil South Witch, granted an audience to Dorothy Gale and her companions at her palace. She revealed the secret power of Dorothy's Silver Shoes so the girl could return home to Kansas, while using the Golden Cap to transport Dorothy's friends to their respective realms. Later, when contacted for help liberating the Emerald City, Glinda determined through her records that the rightful ruler was Princess Ozma. Glinda marched her army to the city, exposed the disguised witch Mombi, chased her across the desert to force a confession, and oversaw Mombi breaking the enchantment that restored Tip to Princess Ozma. After assisting Ozma in reclaiming the throne, Glinda continued to offer her counsel, later advising Dorothy and Ozma on how to safely send Dorothy to Australia using the Magic Belt. She subsequently attended Princess Ozma's grand birthday celebration, participating in the festive procession alongside the kingdom's other notable figures.

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “By means of the Golden Cap I shall command the Winged Monkeys to carry you to the gates of the Emerald City,” said Glinda, “for it would be a shame to deprive the people of so wonderful a ruler.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: "yet I cannot understand how I have been defeated so easily by an old Witch who knows far less of magic than I do myself."

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “That is true,” replied the Sorceress, slowly. “But the Emerald City is now ruled by General Jinjur, who has caused herself to be proclaimed Queen. What right have I to oppose her?”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “Then,” decided Glinda, “I will march with my army to the Emerald City, and take Mombi prisoner. After that we can, perhaps, force her to tell the truth about Ozma.”

label: Quote
value: Glinda said: “I am quite obstinate myself,” returned the Sorceress, with a sweet smile. “so I do not fear Mombi in the least. Today I will make all necessary preparations, and we will march upon the Emerald City at daybreak tomorrow.”

label: History
value: The Great Oz is known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler.
unit: Known to the inhabitants of the land as a powerful ruler, the Great Oz requires visitors to the Emerald City to wear green-tinted spectacles before granting them individual audiences in his palace. When Dorothy and her companions seek his help, he assumes a different magical form for each visitor—appearing as a giant Head, a winged Lady, a five-eyed Beast, and a Ball of Fire—and refuses to fulfill their wishes until they destroy the Wicked Witch of the West. Upon their return, Toto knocks over a screen in the throne room, exposing Oz as a non-magical ventriloquist and ordinary man from Omaha. After admitting he is a humbug who has been deceiving everyone, he promises to grant the group's requests the next day.

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I have fooled everyone so long that I thought I should never be found out. It was a great mistake my ever letting you into the Throne Room. Usually I will not see even my subjects, and so they believe I am something terrible."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I can throw the sound of my voice wherever I wish, so that you thought it was coming out of the Head. Here are the other things I used to deceive you."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "When I grew up I became a ventriloquist, and at that I was very well trained by a great master. I can imitate any kind of a bird or beast."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I’m not much of a magician, as I said; but if you will come to me tomorrow morning, I will stuff your head with brains. I cannot tell you how to use them, however; you must find that out for yourself."

label: Quote
value: Great Oz said: "I think you are wrong to want a heart. It makes most people unhappy. If you only knew it, you are in luck not to have a heart."

label: History
value: The Guardian served as the gatekeeper of the Emerald City.
unit: The Guardian served as the gatekeeper of the Emerald City, responsible for locking green-tinted spectacles onto travelers, such as Dorothy's party, before leading them inside to seek an audience with Oz. He later greeted Jack Pumpkinhead and the Saw-Horse at the city gates to fit them with spectacles and escort them inside. During General Jinjur's rebellion, Jinjur's all-female Army of Revolt overpowered the Guardian at the gates using knitting needles to capture the Emerald City. He eventually resumed his duties at the entrance, greeting Dorothy and her party when they returned to the city in Princess Ozma's royal chariot.

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Don’t try, my dear,” he answered. “We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way.”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Ouch!” cried the man; “I’m sorry I asked that question. But the answer is most convincing. Have you any errand, sir, in the Emerald City?”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: "Here is a strange gentleman who doesn’t know why he has come to the Emerald City, or what he wants. Tell me, what shall we do with him?"

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “I haven’t a pair in stock that will really cover those eyes up,” said the little man, with a sigh; “and your head is so big that I shall be obliged to tie the spectacles on.”

label: Quote
value: Guardian said: “Good gracious!” returned the surprised Guardian of the Gates; “what a nonsensical idea! Go home to your mothers, my good girls, and milk the cows and bake the bread. Don’t you know it’s a dangerous thing to conquer a city?”

label: History
value: Before his head was used to construct a flying machine, the Gump was a monarch of the forest.
unit: Before his head was used to construct a flying machine, the Gump was a monarch of the forest who possessed legs that carried him swiftly until he was killed and mounted on a wall. Tip eventually brought the assembled machine to life using the Powder of Life, animating the Gump's head to serve as its leader. After having its broken wings repaired with a wishing pill, the Gump flew Tip and his companions across the desert to pursue Mombi, ultimately helping Glinda capture the witch and carry her back to camp. During an aerial assault on the Emerald City to depose General Jinjur, the Gump flew Princess Ozma into the city, and once order was restored, it requested to be dismantled. Its head was placed back on a palace wall, where it was later visited by Dorothy before breakfast with Ozma.

label: Appearance
value: The Saw-Horse is an animated wooden steed.
unit: The Saw-Horse is an animated wooden steed featuring a body made from a log with four stiff, stick legs driven into bored holes, lacking knee-joints and shod with plates of solid gold that act as golden hoofs. Its head is formed from a hard wooden knot projecting from one end of the log body, complete with a chopped-out mouth, queer protruding knotty eyes that blink, and no ears. A small tree branch left on the log by accident serves as the creature's tail. Overall, this mere thing of wood is smaller and more natural in appearance than larger beasts, despite its long back and rigid structure.

unit: The Saw-Horse is an extraordinarily swift wooden creature whose legs move fast enough to outrun the wind. Incapable of feeling pain, fatigue, or the need to eat and breathe, the horse displays remarkable physical endurance and can trot as fast as Jim. Initially noted by others as obstinate and stupid, the horse has also been described as very wise and patient over time. Highly obedient to commands, the Saw-Horse acts without hesitation and does not know what danger means, remaining consistently brave and fearless.

label: History
value: The wooden Saw-Horse was brought to life by Tip using Mombi's magic powder.
unit: Brought to life by Tip using Mombi's magic powder, the wooden Saw-Horse was given carved ears so it could hear commands and speak, as well as a post hammered into its back to serve as a handhold. While carrying Jack Pumpkinhead to the Emerald City, the Saw-Horse ran so quickly that its tail snapped off in Tip's hands. It later carried Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow away from Jinjur's army into a wide river, eventually transporting the companions to the palace of the Tin Woodman. During their journey, the Saw-Horse broke its leg in a rabbit hole, which was repaired using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs at the Woggle-Bug's suggestion. It later helped figure out the counting requirement needed to activate Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills while the party was stranded in a giant Jackdaw nest. During the pursuit of Mombi, Glinda rode the Saw-Horse across the desert to chase down the witch after she transformed into a massive Griffin. Fitted with gold-plated hooves by Ozma so its wooden legs would not wear out, the Saw-Horse eventually met Jim the horse in the Emerald City and defeated him in a race, after which Ozma crowned it the Prince of Horses. It later attended the grand birthday festivities for Princess Ozma alongside the Scarecrow and other guests.

unit: Brought to life by Tip using Mombi's magic powder, the wooden Saw-Horse was given carved ears so it could hear commands and speak, as well as a post hammered into its back to serve as a handhold. While carrying Jack Pumpkinhead to the Emerald City, the Saw-Horse ran so quickly that its tail snapped off in Tip's hands. It later carried Tip, Jack, and the Scarecrow away from Jinjur's army into a wide river, eventually transporting the companions to the palace of the Tin Woodman. During their journey, the Saw-Horse broke its leg in a rabbit hole, which was repaired using one of Jack Pumpkinhead's legs at the Woggle-Bug's suggestion. It later helped figure out the counting requirement needed to activate Dr. Nikidik's Wishing Pills while the party was stranded in a giant Jackdaw nest. During the pursuit of Mombi, Glinda rode the Saw-Horse across the desert to chase down the witch after she transformed into a massive Griffin. Fitted with gold-plated hooves by Ozma so its wooden legs would not wear out, the Saw-Horse eventually met Jim the horse in the Emerald City and defeated him in a race, after which Ozma crowned it the Prince of Horses. It later attended the grand birthday festivities for Princess Ozma alongside the Scarecrow and other guests.

label: Quote
value: Horse said: “Well, I cannot claim any great experience in life,” the Saw-Horse answered for himself. “but I seem to learn very quickly, and often it occurs to me that I know more than any of those around me.”

label: Quote
value: Horse said: "Oh, no," answered the Sawhorse. "I merely said it wasn't fair. But if my friend the Real Horse is willing to undertake the race I am quite ready."

label: Quote
value: Horse said: "I couldn't help it," returned the other, rather crestfallen. "Ozma sprinkled me with a magic powder, and I just had to live. I know I'm not much account; but I'm the only horse in all the Land of Oz, so they treat me with great respect."

label: Quote
value: Horse said: "Oh, I cannot hope ever to be like you," sighed the Sawhorse. "But I am glad to meet at last a Real Horse. You are certainly the most beautiful creature I ever beheld."

label: Quote
value: Horse said: "I can see the bones all right," replied the Sawhorse, "and they are admirable and distinct. Also I can see the flesh. But the blood, I suppose, is tucked away inside."

Following her ascension, the Saw-Horse remains a steadfast ally to the new ruler of Oz.

label: History
value: The Hungry Tiger was born with an unfulfillable appetite.
unit: Born with an unfulfillable appetite, the Hungry Tiger left the forest to join his friend, the Cowardly Lion. He accompanied Princess Ozma, Dorothy Gale, and their companions on a quest to the Nome King's underground realm to rescue the bartered royal family of Ev. During the expedition, the Hungry Tiger helped defend Dorothy when the enraged Nome King ordered his army to capture her. Following their victory, he traveled to the Emerald City, where Dorothy was named a Princess of Oz. During a subsequent grand celebration in the Emerald City, the Tiger knocked over Jim the horse after Jim angrily kicked the Sawhorse following a race. Later, the Hungry Tiger and the Cowardly Lion brought Princess Ozma's royal chariot to convey Dorothy and her party into the city for Ozma's grand birthday banquet and festival.

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "For my part, I'm a savage beast, and have an appetite for all sorts of poor little living creatures, from a chipmonk to fat babies."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "My, my! how good you would taste if I could only crunch you between my jaws. But don't worry. You would only appease my appetite for a moment; so it isn't worth while to eat you."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "you'll ruin my reputation if you are not more discreet. It isn't what we are, but what folks think we are, that counts in this world. And come to think of it Miss Polly would make a fine variegated breakfast, I'm sure."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "Then," said the Tiger, yawning frightfully, "please to get me about thirty pounds of tenderloin steak, cooked rare, with a peck of boiled potatoes on the side, and five gallons of ice-cream for dessert."

label: Quote
value: Hungry Tiger said: "A bushel of them, hard boiled, might take a little of the edge off my appetite; but one egg isn't good for anything at all, that I know of."

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in the Gillikin region of Oz.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was created in the Gillikin region of Oz when a young boy named Tip carved a pumpkin for his head, constructed a wooden body, and dressed him in old clothes. Shortly after, the sorceress Mombi brought Jack to life using the magic Powder of Life. Fearing Mombi's wrath, Tip fled with Jack toward the Emerald City, animating a wooden Saw-Horse along the way so Jack would have a steed to ride. Jack was separated from Tip during the journey and arrived first at the Emerald City, where he met the Scarecrow King and became his friend after clearing up an initial misunderstanding. When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt invaded the city, Jack fled alongside Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman, during which one of Jack's wooden legs was removed to repair the Saw-Horse's broken limb.

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “My name is Jack Pumpkinhead,” returned the other, smilingly; “but as to my business, I haven’t the least idea in the world what it is.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “It seems to me that I have,” replied the Pumpkinhead, seriously; “but I cannot think what it is. My father knows all about it, but he is not here.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “But I hope she cannot get at us,” exclaimed the Pumpkinhead, with a shiver of fear. “She threatened to make tarts of me, you know.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “Oh, dear!” moaned Jack; “what an unhappy lot is mine! Why, dear father, did you not make me out of tin—or even out of straw—so that I would keep indefinitely.”

label: Quote
value: Jack Pumpkinhead said: “First, however,” said the Pumpkinhead, “I beg you will release me from this horse, and make me another leg to walk with. For in my present condition I am of no use to myself or to anyone else.”

label: History
value: Jellia Jamb was born in the North Country.
unit: Jellia Jamb, who was born in the North Country, served as a maid in the Emerald City palace, where she initially played a trick by acting as a fake interpreter between Jack Pumpkinhead and the Scarecrow. During Jinjur's rebellion, Mombi magically disguised Jellia as herself in an attempt to fool Glinda, though Glinda immediately saw through the deception. She continued her duties at the palace, later welcoming the Wizard, Zeb, and Jim upon their arrival, and subsequently greeting Dorothy and her traveling companions to direct them to their rooms for Ozma's banquet.

label: Quote
value: Jellia Jamb said: "Why not, Mr. Wizard?" asked Jellia, bowing low. "But I'm afraid you cannot rule the Emerald City, as you used to, because we now have a beautiful Princess whom everyone loves dearly."

label: Quote
value: Jellia Jamb said: "She is with the Princess Ozma, in the private rooms of the palace," replied Jellia Jamb. "But she has ordered me to make you welcome and to show you to your apartments."

label: Quote
value: Jellia Jamb said: “Because they are one and the same!” declared the girl, now laughing merrily. “Does not your Majesty know that in all the land of Oz but one language is spoken?”

label: Quote
value: Jellia Jamb said: "We have never needed them before," answered Jellia; "for the Sawhorse lives in a room of the palace, being much smaller and more natural in appearance than this great beast you have brought with you."

label: Quote
value: Jellia Jamb said: "Oh, no," she hastened to say, "there may be many more like you in the place you came from, but in Oz any horse but a Sawhorse is unusual."

label: History
value: Jim was born in Kentucky.
unit: Born in Kentucky, Jim was a former race horse who won every race in his youth before spending years drawing a public cab in Chicago. Treated as a servant since birth, he was pulling a buggy with Zeb to meet Dorothy when a sudden earthquake plunged them, along with the buggy, into an underground abyss. During their descent to a subterranean city of glass, Jim gained the ability to speak. After the native Mangaboos attempted to banish the group's animals to the Black Pit, Jim fought fiercely, but he and the others were cornered in a cave before escaping through a mountain tunnel. Jim pulled the buggy across dangerous underground lands, kicked at attacking wooden Gargoyles, and flew the group to safety using stolen wooden wings wired to his body and the buggy. Trapped in a dead-end cave, Jim and his companions were rescued when Princess Ozma magically transported them to the Emerald City. In Oz, Jim demanded raw oatmeal, met the Sawhorse, and was beaten by the Sawhorse in a public race; in anger, Jim kicked his opponent and was knocked over by the Hungry Tiger. Ultimately, Ozma used her Magic Belt to return Jim and Zeb back to Hugson's Ranch.

label: Quote
value: Jim said: "Bah!" cried Jim, looking with great disdain at the other; "do you imagine for an instant that such a shabby imitation of a horse as you are can run as fast as I?"

label: Quote
value: Jim said: "Once, when I was young," said Jim, "I was a race horse, and defeated all who dared run against me. I was born in Kentucky, you know, where all the best and most aristocratic horses come from."

label: Quote
value: Jim said: "Old! Why, I feel like a colt today," replied Jim. "I only wish there was a real horse here for me to race with. I'd show the people a fine sight, I can tell you."

label: Quote
value: Jim said: "I beg your pardon, I'm sure," said Jim, meekly. "I was wrong to kick the Sawhorse, and I am sorry I became angry at him. He has won the race, and won it fairly; but what can a horse of flesh do against a tireless beast of wood?"

label: Quote
value: Jim said: "I ought to be a fairy," grumbled Jim, as he slowly drew the buggy home; "for to be just an ordinary horse in a fairy country is to be of no account whatever. It's no place for us, Zeb."

After this conversation, Dorothy's party carefully travels through the region and exits over the opposite wall.

label: History
value: Princess Langwidere was a niece of King Evoldo
unit: Princess Langwidere was a niece of the late King Evoldo who ruled the Land of Ev and possessed thirty changeable heads stored in a cabinet. When Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina arrived at her palace, Langwidere put on an ill-tempered head and demanded Dorothy's head for her collection; upon Dorothy's refusal, Langwidere had her army arrest the group and locked Dorothy in the North Tower. Princess Ozma of Oz later arrived at the palace and forced Langwidere to release Dorothy and her companions. When Ozma organized an expedition to rescue Ev's royal family from the Nome King, Langwidere declined to join the quest, remaining behind at her palace where she was eventually present when Prince Evardo was crowned the new King of Ev.

label: Quote
value: Langwidere said: "This head with the auburn hair and hazel eyes is quite attractive. I must wear it more often than I have done of late, although it may not be the best of my collection."

label: Quote
value: Langwidere said: "How dare you enter my palace unbidden? Leave this room at once, or I will bind you and all your people in chains, and throw you into my darkest dungeons!"

label: Quote
value: Langwidere said: "I had forgotten all about her. That was yesterday, you know, and a Princess cannot be expected to remember today what she did yesterday. Come with me, and I will release the prisoner at once."

label: Quote
value: Langwidere said: "Huh!" cried the Princess, scornfully. "You are a foolish child, and I cannot allow you to annoy me. Run away, you little goose, and bother some one else."

label: Quote
value: Langwidere said: "Then," said Langwidere, "I shall lock you up in a tower until you decide to obey me. Nanda," turning to her maid, "call my army."

label: History
value: Mombi was an old witch.
unit: Mombi was an old witch living in the Gillikin region of Oz who had previously received magical tricks from the Wizard of Oz, obtained the Powder of Life from a crooked sorcerer, served as jailor to Princess Ozma's grandfather and father, and transformed the baby Princess Ozma into a young boy named Tip, whom she raised under her care. After returning home from a trip with the Powder of Life, Mombi animated Tip's wooden creation, Jack Pumpkinhead, and brewed a potion intending to transform Tip into a marble statue, which prompted Tip to steal her magical powder and escape. Jinjur later summoned Mombi to aid her rebellion against the Scarecrow, leading Mombi to conjure magical illusions such as whirling sunflowers to hinder Tip and his traveling companions. When Glinda's army surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to avoid capture by disguising Jellia Jamb as herself, then transforming into a red rose, and subsequently shifting through various animal forms before collapsing in the desert and being captured by Glinda. Brought to Glinda's tent and questioned under a truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip, and she was forced to perform the incantation that restored Ozma to her true form.

When Glinda's army surrounded the Emerald City, Mombi attempted to avoid capture by disguising Jellia Jamb as herself, then transforming into a red rose, and subsequently shifting through various animal forms before collapsing in the desert and being captured by Glinda. Brought to Glinda's tent and questioned under a truth-detecting pearl, Mombi confessed that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip, and she was forced to perform the incantation that restored Ozma to her true form.

label: History
value: Nick Chopper was born a real man made of flesh and bones.
unit: Born a real man made of flesh and bones, Nick Chopper earned his living as a woodcutter until repeated axe accidents forced him to replace his limbs with tin until no flesh remained. After receiving a lovely heart from the Wizard, he became the Emperor of the Winkies. When his friend the Scarecrow sought his aid against a rebellion in the Emerald City, Nick Chopper joined the journey, helping repair Jack Pumpkinhead's leg and constructing a flying machine known as the Gump on the palace roof. During a later battle with Mombi, the Sorceress Glinda discovered that the rose worn by Nick Chopper was actually the transformed witch in disguise. Later, while traveling with Princess Ozma's procession in Ev, he was turned into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King before being restored by Billina. Back in his realm, he warmly welcomed Dorothy and her companions to his magnificent tin castle, hosting a grand dinner before agreeing to accompany them toward the Emerald City.

During a later battle with Mombi, the Sorceress Glinda discovered that the rose worn by Nick Chopper was actually the transformed witch in disguise. Later, while traveling with Princess Ozma's procession in Ev, he was turned into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King before being restored by Billina. Back in his realm, he warmly welcomed Dorothy and her companions to his magnificent tin castle, hosting a grand dinner before agreeing to accompany them toward the Emerald City.

label: History
value: Ozma was reared from childhood by Mombi.
unit: Reared from childhood by the witch Mombi, Ozma was originally transformed into a boy named Tip so that her true identity as the rightful Princess of the Land of Oz would remain hidden. After escaping Mombi with Jack Pumpkinhead, Tip brought the Sawhorse and the Gump to life using magic powder. When Glinda the Good marched on the Emerald City and captured Mombi, the witch was forced to reverse the enchantment, restoring Ozma to her rightful female form as Princess. Following an aerial assault to quash General Jinjur's revolt, Ozma was crowned Queen of the Emerald City. She later led an expedition to Ev and the Nome King's realm to rescue Ev's royal family, but she was transformed into an emerald grasshopper ornament when she failed the King's guessing game. After being restored by Billina, Ozma returned victorious to Oz alongside Dorothy, whom she made a Princess. When Dorothy later needed to return home, Ozma used the Nome King's Magic Belt to send her away, and she later offered the Wizard a permanent home as Official Wizard of Oz. Ozma eventually manipulated the roads to guide Dorothy and her companions back to the Emerald City, where she welcomed them, pardoned the shaggy man, and hosted a magnificent birthday banquet attended by dignitaries from across the world.

value: The Scarecrow is a light-weight stuffed man.

His hands consist of white, padded, squashy gloves filled with straw, and he features a straw-padded bosom and straw-stuffed shoulders. His head is a small sack stuffed with straw, bulged out at the top with brains, featuring a painted face complete with eyes, ears, a nose, and a lovely painted smile that has no swallow connected to it. Upon his head, he wears a heavy golden crown set thick with sparkling jewels, though he is also noted as being solid gold.

label: Personality
value: Scarecrow is widely acknowledged as the most popular man in all the Land of Oz.
unit: This celebrated personage is widely acknowledged as the most popular, beloved, and wisest man in all the Land of Oz. Happy, gay, and charming in his expression, he maintains his personal dignity while remaining calm under all circumstances. He possesses a thoughtful and philosophical nature, firmly believing that brains are far superior to money. Being stuffed with straw, he requires neither food nor sleep, and his unique eyes allow him to see as well in the dark as during the day. His early journey was driven by a deep desire to seek brains from the Great Oz so he could become like other men, alongside a selfless determination to help his friend Dorothy return home to Kansas. The only thing in the world he fears is fire or a lighted match, as a single spark could easily burn his straw body to ash.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow was created by a Munchkin farmer.
unit: Created by a Munchkin farmer and stuffed with straw, the Scarecrow was removed from his cornfield pole by Dorothy Gale and agreed to travel with her to the Emerald City to ask Oz for brains. Along the yellow brick road, he helped rescue the Tin Woodman, braved attacks by Kalidahs, and devised clever plans to safely cross chasms and escape a deadly poppy field with the aid of field mice. Upon reaching the Emerald City, he faced Oz's varied disguises and was sent to defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, during which he was torn apart by Winged Monkeys before being re-stuffed by Winkie tinsmiths. Returning to Oz, he discovered the ruler was a fraud but nevertheless received a brain of bran and pins from the Wizard, who appointed him King of the Emerald City upon departing. When General Jinjur's army later deposed him, he escaped on the Sawhorse, recruited the Tin Woodman, and ultimately helped Princess Ozma claim her rightful throne. He subsequently joined Ozma on a dangerous expedition to the Nome King's underground realm, where he was temporarily transformed into an ornament before being restored and helping defeat the Nomes. Later residing peacefully in Oz, he joined in welcoming Dorothy back on her subsequent visits, participated in Eureka's murder trial, and helped celebrate Princess Ozma's grand birthday festival.

label: History
value: The Shaggy Man is a homeless wanderer.
unit: A homeless wanderer who previously stole a magical Love Magnet from a girl in Butterfield, the Shaggy Man met Dorothy and became lost with her while traveling toward Butterfield. He joined Dorothy, Toto, and several other lost companions on a journey toward the Emerald City, using his Love Magnet to gain favor with characters like King Dox and to summon Johnny Dooit to build a sand-boat across the deadly desert. After receiving a donkey head from King Kik-a-bray, he was eventually restored to his normal human form by diving into the Truth Pond. Upon arriving in the Emerald City, he confessed his theft of the Love Magnet to Princess Ozma, who placed the artifact over the city gates before welcoming him to stay for her birthday celebration.

label: Quote
value: Shaggy Man said: "The Truth Pond. Now, at last, I may get rid of this frightful head; for we were told, you remember, that only the Truth Pond could restore to me my proper face."

label: Quote
value: Shaggy Man said: "It is, indeed," replied the shaggy man. "I hated dreadfully to go to Princess Ozma looking like this; and she's to have a birthday celebration, too."

label: Quote
value: Shaggy Man said: "I may not be strictly beautiful, even now," he said to his companions, who watched him with smiling faces; "but I'm so much handsomer than any donkey that I feel as proud as I can be."

label: Quote
value: Shaggy Man said: "I hate to leave it," murmured the shaggy man, with a sigh. "A truth pond wouldn't be a bad thing to carry around with us."

label: Quote
value: Shaggy Man said: "we find that we can't cross this desert, which turns all living flesh that touches it into dust; so I have asked you to come and help us."

label: Dorothy
value: Dorothy and the Shaggy Man became traveling companions.
unit: Dorothy and the Shaggy Man became traveling companions after he asked her for directions to Butterfield and they accidentally became lost at a magical crossroads. value: A crooked Sorcerer invented the Magic Powder of Life.

His two halves were subsequently carried to a field by a procession to be planted.

label: History
value: The King acquired a long life.
unit: The King acquired a long life by purchasing the family of King Evoldo, whom he subsequently enslaved and transformed into decorative ornaments for his underground palace. When Ozma arrived demanding their release, the King lured her and her followers into a high-stakes guessing game that resulted in their transformation into ornaments as well. His victory was overturned when the hen Billina discovered his secret, disenchanted his prisoners, and exploited his mortal terror of eggs to panic his army. Blinded by egg yolks, the King was forced to yield his magic belt to Dorothy, stripping him of his power as the captives escaped.

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Sit down, my dears," said the King, "and tell me why you have come all this way to see me, and what I can do to make you happy."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Oh, no; you are mistaken about that," replied the King. "They are not my prisoners, but my slaves, whom I purchased from the King of Ev."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "According to the laws of Ev, the king can do no wrong," answered the monarch, eyeing a ring of smoke he had just blown from his mouth; "so that he had a perfect right to sell his family to me in exchange for a long life."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "That was not my fault," said the Nome King, crossing his legs and smiling contentedly. "I gave him the long life, all right; but he destroyed it."

label: Quote
value: The King said: "Of course not," the Nome King returned. "Nor will I give up the Queen and her children because the King of Ev destroyed his long life by jumping into the sea. They belong to me and I shall keep them."

label: History
value: Tiktok is a copper clockwork man.
unit: Tiktok is a copper clockwork man constructed in Evna by Smith & Tinker, who fitted him with Improved Combination Steel Brains. He is discovered locked in a rock doorway by Dorothy Gale and Billina, who wind up his mechanical mechanisms for thinking, speaking, and action. After pledging his service to Dorothy, Tiktok defends her from the Wheelers using a tin dinner pail and guides her toward Evna. When Princess Langwidere orders Dorothy's arrest, Tiktok attempts to protect the girl until his action runs down, resulting in Dorothy's imprisonment before Princess Ozma arrives to secure her release. Joining Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev, Tiktok travels to the Nome King's underground realm and takes his turn making guesses in the King's ornament palace, but his mechanism runs down before he fails and is transformed into a green ornament. He is later freed from the curse when Billina uncovers the secret to restoring the transformed prisoners. Following their victory over the Nome King, Tiktok travels with the group back through Ev and across the desert to the Emerald City, where he celebrates Dorothy's appointment as a Princess of Oz and bids her farewell upon her departure for Australia.

unit: Tiktok is a copper clockwork man constructed in Evna by Smith & Tinker, who fitted him with Improved Combination Steel Brains. He is discovered locked in a rock doorway by Dorothy Gale and Billina, who wind up his mechanical mechanisms for thinking, speaking, and action. After pledging his service to Dorothy, Tiktok defends her from the Wheelers using a tin dinner pail and guides her toward Evna. When Princess Langwidere orders Dorothy's arrest, Tiktok attempts to protect the girl until his action runs down, resulting in Dorothy's imprisonment before Princess Ozma arrives to secure her release. Joining Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev, Tiktok travels to the Nome King's underground realm and takes his turn making guesses in the King's ornament palace, but his mechanism runs down before he fails and is transformed into a green ornament. He is later freed from the curse when Billina uncovers the secret to restoring the transformed prisoners. Following their victory over the Nome King, Tiktok travels with the group back through Ev and across the desert to the Emerald City, where he celebrates Dorothy's appointment as a Princess of Oz and bids her farewell upon her departure for Australia.

value: Tiktok said: "You did not wind me much, at first," he calmly said, "and I told you that long sto-ry a-bout King Ev-ol-do; so it is no won-der that I ran down."

label: Quote
value: Tiktok said: "No; I am the on-ly au-to-mat-ic me-chan-i-cal man they ev-er com-plet-ed," he replied. "They were ver-y won-der-ful in-ven-tors, were my mak-ers, and quite ar-tis-tic in all they did."

label: Quote
value: Tiktok said: "He was," acknowledged Tiktok. "Also he is a great loss to me. For if I should get out of or-der I do not know of an-y one a-ble to re-pair me, be-cause I am so com-pli-cat-ed. You have no i-de-a how full of ma-chin-er-y I am."

label: Quote

value: Tiktok said: "Be kind e-nough to fol-low me," he said, "and I will lead you a-way from here to the town of Ev-na, where you will be more com-for-ta-ble, and also I will pro-tect you from the Wheel-ers."

label: Appearance
value: The Tin Woodman is a tall figure.
unit: The Tin Woodman is a tall, angular figure composed entirely of pieces of tin, neatly soldered and riveted together into the form of a man, with cleverly hinged limbs. His entire body is brilliantly polished and beautifully nickel-plated, causing his nickel cheeks to shine magnificently. He wears a funnel-shaped cap tipped carelessly over his left ear, carries a gleaming axe over his right shoulder, and is adorned with a diamond necklace.

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman is a simple figure.
unit: The Tin Woodman is a simple, proud, and cheerful figure who is widely regarded as a popular favorite among the people. Known for his exceptionally kind, loving, and sensitive nature, he is deeply averse to killing and is always careful to avoid causing harm to any living creature. He holds a fondness for both children and flowers, and he displays a marked lack of vanity despite his patched metallic appearance. Driven by a desire to obtain a heart from Oz so he can love and marry a Munchkin maiden, he values a good heart above both education and brains, willingly accepting any potential unhappiness it might bring. His journey is also motivated by a wish to help Dorothy, a goal to reach the Emerald City, and an ambition to return to the Country of the West to rule forever over the Winkies, to whom he is fond. In addition to his fine nature, he is a skillful mechanic and possesses a notable talent for swinging his axe with incredible speed.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was originally a man of flesh and bone.
unit: The Tin Woodman, originally a man of flesh and bone who chopped wood for a living, was cursed by the Wicked Witch of the East, causing his axe to slice away his limbs; he replaced each lost body part with tin until he was made entirely of metal and lost his heart. After standing rusted in a forest for a year, he was discovered and oiled by Dorothy and the Scarecrow, joining them on a quest to the Emerald City to request a heart from the Great Oz. Along their journey along the yellow brick road, he fought off threats by chopping down trees to stop pursuing Kalidahs and slaying a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, later building a wooden truck so her mice could haul the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of a deadly poppy field. When Oz commanded the group to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before granting their wishes, the Tin Woodman traveled west, only to be dismantled by the Witch's Winged Monkeys. Following the Witch's defeat, grateful Winkie tinsmiths repaired his body, and he was later granted a silk heart by Oz before helping Dorothy travel south to seek Glinda's counsel. The Winkies subsequently made him their Emperor, prompting him to construct a new tin house in their country to prevent his joints from rusting in his old damp castle. When Princess Ozma was overthrown by General Jinjur's revolt, he joined the Scarecrow to help reclaim the Emerald City, accidentally carrying the disguised witch Mombi back to camp in the form of a plucked red rose before Ozma was successfully restored to the throne. Later, he joined Ozma's expedition across the desert to the Nome King's realm to rescue the royal family of Ev, where he was temporarily transformed into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King before being restored by Billina's magic. Upon returning to Oz, he reunited with the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City and stood defense for Dorothy's kitten Eureka during a murder trial, even offering a spare piglet from his hat to save the kitten from execution. While residing in his realm in the Winkie Country, he welcomed Dorothy and her traveling party to his tin castle and guided them back toward the Emerald City, stopping to show them Jack Pumpkinhead's home along the way. Upon reaching the capital, he participated in the grand birthday banquet and festival hosted by Princess Ozma.

unit: The Tin Woodman, originally a man of flesh and bone who chopped wood for a living, was cursed by the Wicked Witch of the East, causing his axe to slice away his limbs; he replaced each lost body part with tin until he was made entirely of metal and lost his heart. After standing rusted in a forest for a year, he was discovered and oiled by Dorothy and the Scarecrow, joining them on a quest to the Emerald City to request a heart from the Great Oz. Along their journey along the yellow brick road, he fought off threats by chopping down trees to stop pursuing Kalidahs and slaying a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, later building a wooden truck so her mice could haul the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of a deadly poppy field. When Oz commanded the group to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before granting their wishes, the Tin Woodman traveled west, only to be dismantled by the Witch's Winged Monkeys. Following the Witch's defeat, grateful Winkie tinsmiths repaired his body, and he was later granted a silk heart by Oz before helping Dorothy travel south to seek Glinda's counsel. The Winkies subsequently made him their Emperor, prompting him to construct a new tin house in their country to prevent his joints from rusting in his old damp castle. When Princess Ozma was overthrown by General Jinjur's revolt, he joined the Scarecrow to help reclaim the Emerald City, accidentally carrying the disguised witch Mombi back to camp in the form of a plucked red rose before Ozma was successfully restored to the throne. Later, he joined Ozma's expedition across the desert to the Nome King's realm to rescue the royal family of Ev, where he was temporarily transformed into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King before being restored by Billina's magic. Upon returning to Oz, he reunited with the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City and stood defense for Dorothy's kitten Eureka during a murder trial, even offering a spare piglet from his hat to save the kitten from execution. While residing in his realm in the Winkie Country, he welcomed Dorothy and her traveling party to his tin castle and guided them back toward the Emerald City, stopping to show them Jack Pumpkinhead's home along the way. Upon reaching the capital, he participated in the grand birthday banquet and festival hosted by Princess Ozma.

unit: The Tin Woodman, originally a man of flesh and bone who chopped wood for a living, was cursed by the Wicked Witch of the East, causing his axe to slice away his limbs; he replaced each lost body part with tin until he was made entirely of metal and lost his heart. After standing rusted in a forest for a year, he was discovered and oiled by Dorothy and the Scarecrow, joining them on a quest to the Emerald City to request a heart from the Great Oz. Along their journey along the yellow brick road, he fought off threats by chopping down trees to stop pursuing Kalidahs and slaying a wildcat to save the Queen of the Field Mice, later building a wooden truck so her mice could haul the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of a deadly poppy field. When Oz commanded the group to destroy the Wicked Witch of the West before granting their wishes, the Tin Woodman traveled west, only to be dismantled by the Witch's Winged Monkeys. Following the Witch's defeat, grateful Winkie tinsmiths repaired his body, and he was later granted a silk heart by Oz before helping Dorothy travel south to seek Glinda's counsel. The Winkies subsequently made him their Emperor, prompting him to construct a new tin house in their country to prevent his joints from rusting in his old damp castle. When Princess Ozma was overthrown by General Jinjur's revolt, he joined the Scarecrow to help reclaim the Emerald City, accidentally carrying the disguised witch Mombi back to camp in the form of a plucked red rose before Ozma was successfully restored to the throne. Later, he joined Ozma's expedition across the desert to the Nome King's realm to rescue the royal family of Ev, where he was temporarily transformed into a tin pig whistle by the Nome King before being restored by Billina's magic. Upon returning to Oz, he reunited with the Wizard of Oz in the Emerald City and stood defense for Dorothy's kitten Eureka during a murder trial, even offering a spare piglet from his hat to save the kitten from execution. While residing in his realm in the Winkie Country, he welcomed Dorothy and her traveling party to his tin castle and guided them back toward the Emerald City, stopping to show them Jack Pumpkinhead's home along the way. Upon reaching the capital, he participated in the grand birthday banquet and festival hosted by Princess Ozma.

label: History
value: Toto lived on a farm in Kansas
unit: Toto lived on a farm in Kansas with Dorothy, Aunt Em, and Uncle Henry, where he enjoyed chasing mice. When a severe cyclone lifted their house into the air, he was carried away with Dorothy to the Land of Oz. After the house landed on the Wicked Witch of the East, Toto accompanied Dorothy and her new companions along the yellow brick road to seek help from the Great Oz. Along the way, he was attacked by a Cowardly Lion, survived a field of sleeping poppies, and accidentally exposed Oz as a humbug by knocking over a screen in the Throne Room. During Oz's attempt to take Dorothy home in a hot-air balloon, Toto ran off into the crowd, causing Dorothy to miss the departure. He then traveled with Dorothy through China country and Quadling territory, eventually returning safely to Kansas when Dorothy activated her magic Silver Shoes. Following a period spent in Australia with Dorothy and Uncle Henry, Toto accompanied Dorothy back through mysterious crossroads. Along the route, Toto discovered two-sided Scoodlers perched on rocks before the group was captured, but they successfully escaped. After crossing the Deadly Desert in a magical sand-boat, Toto returned to the Land of Oz, met Princess Ozma at the Emerald City, and eventually prepared to be transported back to Kansas with Dorothy using the Magic Belt.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch ruled over the Winkies in the West.
unit: The Wicked Witch ruled over the Winkies in the West from her castle and held a power over them through force and magical artifacts. When Dorothy and her companions traveled west to destroy her, the Witch spotted them and dispatched waves of wolves, crows, bees, and Winkie soldiers to destroy the group. After those attempts failed, she used the Golden Cap to command the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, capture the Lion, and bring Dorothy to her castle as a servant. After tricking Dorothy into losing one of her silver shoes, an argument broke out that led Dorothy to throw a bucket of water on the Witch, causing her to melt away completely and ending her tyranny.

label: Personality
value: The Wizard is renowned for his wisdom.
unit: The Wizard is a complex figure renowned for his wisdom and potential for destruction, yet he candidly admits to being a humbug and a very bad Wizard rather than a true magician. Characterized as a jolly and good fellow, he relies heavily on sleight-of-hand, juggling, and circus-learned tricks, though he is also capable of animal training, inventing unique machines, and performing magic displays. He possesses the reputed ability to shapeshift into any form he wishes. Driven by practical motivations, he seeks to escape a cavern before a mother dragon returns and longs to find a path back to the earth's surface. Ultimately, he desires to return to Kansas to resume his former life in a circus.

label: History
value: The Wizard was born in Omaha.
unit: Born in Omaha as the son of a politician, the Wizard originally ran away from home to join a circus, where he practiced ventriloquism, learned magic tricks from jugglers, and drew crowds by ascending in a balloon. During one balloon flight, his ropes twisted and carried him away to Oz, where he was mistaken for a mighty sorcerer, usurped the throne from King Pastoria, gave the infant Princess Ozma to the witch Mombi to hide, and commanded the local people to build the Emerald City and his royal palace. Years later, he attempted to return to Kansas with Dorothy in a newly built hot-air balloon, but accidentally floated away alone when the ropes snapped early. He eventually fell through an earthquake fissure into the glass world of the Mangaboos, where he reunited with Dorothy, defeated the local sorcerer Gwig, and used burning kerosene to intimidate the Mangaboo Princess before being sealed inside the Black Pit. Escaping upward through underground tunnels, he helped defend the group during their travels through the Valley of Voe, Pyramid Mountain, and the wooden Country of the Gargoyles until Princess Ozma magically transported them out of a dead-end cave to the Emerald City. Ozma offered him a permanent home as Official Wizard, and during Eureka's murder trial he attempted to secret a spare piglet to clear the kitten's name before the lost piglet was safely recovered. He later joined Dorothy, Polychrome, and the shaggy man in reuniting with Princess Ozma, entertaining guests with magic tricks and utilizing his giant soap-bubble machine during Ozma's grand birthday festival.

label: History
value: Zeb was a farm worker.
unit: Zeb was a farm worker who was driving Dorothy to Hugson's Ranch in a buggy drawn by his horse, Jim, when an earthquake caused the ground to split and plunged them all into a subterranean chasm. After floating down into an underground glass city, Zeb and his companions were accused of causing the earthquake damage and eventually trapped in the dark Black Pit by the local Mangaboo people. They escaped upward through a mountain tunnel into the Valley of Voe and journeyed to Pyramid Mountain, ascending its interior stairs until reaching the wooden Country of the Gargoyles. When the silent Gargoyles captured the group, Zeb bravely snuck out while the creatures slept to steal eight unhooked wooden wings, which were then attached to Jim and the buggy so the travelers could fly away. After navigating further caverns and reaching a dead end, Princess Ozma used her Magic Belt to rescue the party, magically transporting Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and the piglets to the Emerald City. While enjoying fine Oz clothes and royal hospitality, Zeb participated in outdoor games where he wrestled and boxed a Munchkin boy. Shortly after helping Dorothy check on their home using Ozma's enchanted picture, Zeb chose to return and was transported by the Magic Belt alongside Jim back to Hugson's Ranch.

After floating down into an underground glass city, Zeb and his companions were accused of causing the earthquake damage and eventually trapped in the dark Black Pit by the local Mangaboo people. They escaped upward through a mountain tunnel into the Valley of Voe and journeyed to Pyramid Mountain, ascending its interior stairs until reaching the wooden Country of the Gargoyles. When the silent Gargoyles captured the group, Zeb bravely snuck out while the creatures slept to steal eight unhooked wooden wings, which were then attached to Jim and the buggy so the travelers could fly away. After navigating further caverns and reaching a dead end, Princess Ozma used her Magic Belt to rescue the party, magically transporting Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and the piglets to the Emerald City. While enjoying fine Oz clothes and royal hospitality, Zeb participated in outdoor games where he wrestled and boxed a Munchkin boy. Shortly after helping Dorothy check on their home using Ozma's enchanted picture, Zeb chose to return and was transported by the Magic Belt alongside Jim back to Hugson's Ranch.

label: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

value: Dorothy and her companions camp in the forest.
chapter: v1 · Chapter VII The Journey to the Great Oz
unit: After camping in the forest, Dorothy and her companions encounter a deep ditch blocking the yellow brick road. The Cowardly Lion carries each traveler across on his back. Later, they face another wide chasm and chop down a tree to form a bridge, but are pursued by fearsome Kalidahs; the Scarecrow orders the tree chopped down just as the beasts cross, sending them into the abyss. Reaching a broad river at the edge of the forest, the group makes camp while the Tin Woodman begins building a raft to cross.

label: v1 · Chapter I The Cyclone
value: Dorothy lives in an environment in Kansas.
unit: Dorothy lives in a drab, gray environment in Kansas with her Uncle Henry, Aunt Em, and her playful dog Toto. A sudden and severe cyclone strikes the farm, prompting Uncle Henry to tend to the livestock and Aunt Em to take shelter in the cyclone cellar. Delayed while retrieving Toto, Dorothy is trapped inside the small house as it is lifted high into the air by the storm, where she eventually relaxes and falls asleep as it floats away.

value: Dorothy wakes up.
chapter: v1 · Chapter V The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy and the Scarecrow wake up and discover the Tin Woodman, rusted motionless in the forest. After Dorothy oils his joints, he joins their journey to the Emerald City in hopes of getting a heart from Oz. As they continue along the yellow brick road, the Tin Woodman recounts how the Wicked Witch of the East cursed his axe, leading to his tin transformation and loss of his heart.

unit: A fierce storm strikes the ship carrying Dorothy and Uncle Henry on their way to Australia. chapter: v3 · The Girl in the Chicken Coop
unit: A fierce storm strikes the ship carrying Dorothy and Uncle Henry on their way to Australia. Fearing her frail uncle has gone on deck in danger, Dorothy goes outside to find him, only to be blown overboard while holding onto a wooden chicken coop. Swept away into the sea, she manages to use the floating coop as a raft and eventually falls asleep once the storm subsides.

chapter: v3 · The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
unit: As Billina repeatedly breaks the Nome King's enchantments, the angry King calls his warriors and tries to capture Dorothy, but the Sawhorse, Lion, and Tiger defend her. When the restored captives emerge, the King declares them prisoners, leading to a brief battle where the Scarecrow throws Billina's eggs at the King. Terrified by the eggs, the Nome army flees in panic, leaving the blinded King helpless as Billina tells Dorothy to seize his magical belt.

value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.

Polychrome happily agrees and enlivens their trek with her cheerful dancing and laughter.

chapter: v5 · ALL PERSONS ARE WARNED NOT TO VENTURE UPON THIS DESERT For the Deadly Sands will Turn Any Living Flesh to Dust in an instant. Beyond This Barrier is the LAND OF OZ But no one can Reach that Beautiful Country because of these Destroying Sands
unit: Stuck at the edge of the deadly desert, the travelers rest for the night before Dorothy and Shaggy Man discuss how to cross into Oz. Using the Love Magnet, Shaggy Man summons Johnny Dooit, who swiftly builds them a magical sand-boat equipped with a sail to safely transport them across the sands. After giving them instructions on how to sail it, Johnny Dooit abruptly vanishes with his chest of tools.

label: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
value: General Jinjur summons Mombi
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

value: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 15. ContentsOLD FRIENDS ARE REUNITED
unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. Zeb gets dressed in fine Oz clothing before attending a dinner with Dorothy, Ozma, and the Wizard, where the Wizard explains his origins and history in Oz. Princess Ozma offers the Wizard a permanent home as Official Wizard, and several of Dorothy's old friends—including the Scarecrow, Billina, Eureka, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—arrive to reunite with them.

unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. label: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
value: General Jinjur summons Mombi.
chapter: v2 · Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.
unit: General Jinjur summons Mombi to help defeat the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, and Mombi uses magic to create a confusing field of whirling, face-bearing sunflowers that delays the travelers. After pushing past the illusion, the Saw-Horse trips in a rabbit hole and breaks its leg, leaving the group stranded while trying to figure out a repair. While sitting in the grass, the group is approached by the Highly Magnified, Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug, who introduces himself and prepares to share his backstory.

value: The Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns.
chapter: v2 · Old Mombi indulges in Witchcraft
unit: While traveling, the Woggle-Bug annoys the group with puns until the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman tell him to restrain himself. Led safely by the Mouse Queen, the travelers overcome the magical obstacles and arrive outside the Emerald City.

value: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City.
chapter: v2 · The Prisoners of the Queen
unit: The Scarecrow and his allies enter the Emerald City and march to the royal palace, where they find General Jinjur occupying the throne. Jinjur signals her Army of Revolt to ambush and disarm the group, threatening them with execution. The Scarecrow releases mice hidden in his straw, causing the female rebels and Jinjur to flee in panic, allowing the group to secure the palace doors.

chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Takes Time to Think
unit: Trapped inside the palace by Jinjur's army, the group despairs over their situation until the Scarecrow devises a plan to escape by air. chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

chapter: v2 · The Tin-Woodman Plucks a Rose
unit: Glinda's army arrives and surrounds the Emerald City, demanding that Queen Jinjur hand over Mombi. unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. value: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country.
chapter: v2 · The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good
unit: The travelers fly on the Gump to the South Country and arrive safely at the palace of Glinda the Good. They seek Glinda's help to liberate the Emerald City, but she explains that the throne rightly belongs to Princess Ozma, who was hidden by the Wizard. After studying her records, Glinda deduces that the old witch Mombi helped hide Ozma, and she resolves to march her army to the Emerald City to capture Mombi and uncover the truth.

unit: Ozma and her companions meet to discuss their quest to free the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, learning how King Evoldo originally bartered them away. unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. Zeb gets dressed in fine Oz clothing before attending a dinner with Dorothy, Ozma, and the Wizard, where the Wizard explains his origins and history in Oz. Princess Ozma offers the Wizard a permanent home as Official Wizard, and several of Dorothy's old friends—including the Scarecrow, Billina, Eureka, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—arrive to reunite with them.

chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 15. ContentsOLD FRIENDS ARE REUNITED
unit: The Wizard, Zeb, and Jim are welcomed to the palace in the Emerald City by Jellia Jamb, and Jim is given a room inside the palace. Zeb gets dressed in fine Oz clothing before attending a dinner with Dorothy, Ozma, and the Wizard, where the Wizard explains his origins and history in Oz. Princess Ozma offers the Wizard a permanent home as Official Wizard, and several of Dorothy's old friends—including the Scarecrow, Billina, Eureka, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—arrive to reunite with them.

chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 18. ContentsTHE TRIAL OF EUREKA THE KITTEN
unit: When one of the Wizard's piglets goes missing from Ozma's room, suspicion falls upon Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Eureka acts defiance and is arrested by Ozma to face trial for murder, leading Ozma to set up a court proceeding and assign roles to their friends. Desperate to spare Dorothy grief, the Wizard gives the Tin Woodman a spare piglet to hide so he can produce it and clear Eureka if she is convicted.

unit: The trial of Eureka takes place in the Throne Room, with the Woggle-Bug prosecuting and the Tin Woodman attempting to defend her. label: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
value: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt.
chapter: v3 · The Fate of the Tin Woodman
unit: Dorothy steals the Nome King's magic belt while he is blinded by egg yolks, stripping him of his power to transform the group into scorpions. Using the belt, Dorothy reopens the passage out of the mountain and threatens the King until he tries to retrieve the transformed Tin Woodman, only to find the object missing. Giving up on finding Nick Chopper, the party escapes through the tunnel, using the belt to fend off pursuing Nome warriors and bypass the iron giant on their way back to Ev.
